text.p: Swiss shares ended firmer but below the highs reached after the release of U.S. jobs data during the second half of the session.
The firmer tendency in the U.S. dollar and the German mark buoyed industrials, dealers said. But sagging bonds toward the end of the session drew the indices down again.
"The market is eagerly awaiting the outcome of U.S. elections on November 5 and will be closely tracking Wall Street until then", one dealer said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 10.9 points, or 0.29 percent, higher at 3,736.2 and the all-share SPI was up 8.73 points to 2,402.78.
Swiss Re was up seven francs to 1,363 after the company released definitive 1995 figures which were within market expectations. Ordinary profit after taxes rose 54 percent in 1995.
Roche led the actives list, advancing 60 francs to 9,620. Second-placed Nestle gave up two francs to end at 1,371.
UBS bearer shares soared six francs to 1,210 after a recent weak spell. Other major banks such as SBC and CS Holding also posted gains.
Among insurers, Winterthur and Zurich were unchanged.
Sulzer reversed an early weak trend, adding nine francs.
SMH bearer shares jumped around 1.94 percent to 790, profiting from a positive story on analyst opinions in the Wall Street Journal, dealers said.
Swissair shook off Thursday's slight losses to end nine francs higher at 994.
Temporary employment firm Adecco was unchanged at 355.
Second-tier shares of freight forwarding group Danzas and participation firm Suedelectra saw good volumes and buying interest on the back on recent recommendations.
Recently sought stocks of medical technology group Stratec fell 47 francs to 1,598.
